unit: dissertations (strict History PhDs, in_analysis: true); never citation counts

caveats: Bibliographies list works consulted, not influence or endorsement.
Before 2009 the corpus is thin and lacks Toronto and York; shown as context only.
Years are mostly repository issued dates, not convocation years.
Laval has 14 PhDs in the graph (downloads pending); francophone coverage relies on Montréal, UQAM and Sherbrooke.
Work matching uses hand-checked graph ids per work; parsing errors can still hide a few citations (undercount, not overcount).

theory.definition: Cites at least one settler-colonial theory work (Wolfe, Veracini, Elkins & Pedersen, Barker & Battell Lowman, Cavanagh & Veracini, Hixson, Mamdani 2001/2020).

core.definition: HEADLINE. Theory works plus Indigenous critique/resurgence works read with them (Coulthard, A. Simpson, Tuck & Yang, Byrd, L. B. Simpson, Kauanui).

core_or_vocabulary.definition: Core, or any cited work whose own title says 'settler colonial(ism)'.

canadian_context.definition: Context only: Canadian historiography of colonial dispossession (Harris, Carter, Perry, Daschuk, Regan, Razack). Much of it predates the paradigm.

critique.definition: Cites a published critique or reassessment of the paradigm (Greer, Ostler & Shoemaker, Shoemaker, Macoun & Strakosch, Snelgrove et al., King).
